subject: Archaeology
title: The Rosetta Stone: Key to Egypt
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Rosetta Stone: Key to Egypt usable.

hook.text: In 1799, French soldiers in Egypt dug up a slab of black stone covered in three scripts.

buildup.text: The stone carried the same decree in hieroglyphs, Demotic, and Greek — a decoder's dream.

discovery.text: Champollion cracked the hieroglyphs in 1822 by matching Greek names to their Egyptian symbols.

twist.text: Egypt has demanded the stone back for decades. Britain has refused every time.

climax.text: That single breakthrough unlocked 3,000 years of Egyptian writing that nobody could read.

punchline.text: A broken slab gave an entire civilization its voice back.

quiz.question: How did Champollion decode hieroglyphs using the Rosetta Stone?
options: He guessed the meaning of each symbol from pictures
He matched Greek names to their Egyptian hieroglyphic equivalents
He used a secret codebook found in a nearby tomb
